claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A simpler definition treats a knowledge graph as a digital structure representing concepts and relationships (facts), and it may include an ontology that lets humans and machines understand and reason about its contents.
claims.quote: A digital structure that represents knowledge as concepts and the relationships between them (facts). A knowledge graph can include an ontology that allows both humans and machines to understand and reason about its contents.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-24)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A knowledge graph formally represents semantics by describing entities and their relationships.
claims.quote: A knowledge graph formally represents semantics by describing entities and their relationships.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-32)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A common knowledge-graph feature is support for reasoning over inferred ontologies: the graph acquires and integrates information into an ontology and applies a reasoner to derive new knowledge.
claims.quote: _Supporting reasoning over inferred ontologies_: A knowledge graph acquires and integrates information into an ontology and applies a reasoner to derive new knowledge.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-Ref1-3)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Virtual knowledge graphs do not store information in specialized databases; they rely on an underlying relational database or data lake and use mappings between the data source elements and the graph structure/ontology.
claims.quote: In contrast, virtual knowledge graphs do not store information in specialized databases.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-30) They rely on an underlying relational database or data lake to answer queries on the graph. Such a virtual knowledge graph system must be properly configured in order to answer the queries correctly. This specific configuration is done through a set of mappings that define the relationship between the elements of the data source and the structure and ontology of the virtual knowledge graph.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-31)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Graph databases allow users to store data as entities and interrelationships and facilitate operations such as data reasoning, node embedding, and ontology development on knowledge bases.
claims.quote: These graph databases allow users to easily store data as entities and their interrelationships, and facilitate operations such as data reasoning, node embedding, and ontology development on knowledge bases.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-29)

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Recent data science and machine learning developments, particularly graph neural networks and representation learning, broadened knowledge-graph scope beyond search engines and recommender systems; knowledge graphs are increasingly used in genomics, proteomics, and systems biology.
claims.quote: Recent developments in data science and [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning"), particularly in [graph neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_neural_network "Graph neural network"), representation learning, and machine learning, have broadened the scope of knowledge graphs beyond their traditional use in search engines and [recommender systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recommender_system "Recommender system"). They are increasingly used in scientific research, with notable applications in fields such as [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics "Genomics"), [proteomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteomics "Proteomics"), and [systems biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_biology "Systems biology").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-5)

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Large language models expanded interest in knowledge graphs as a way to structure information from unstructured text, with language-processing advances enabling automatic or semi-automatic generation and expansion of graphs.
claims.quote: The development of large language models expanded interest in knowledge graphs as a way to structure information from unstructured text, with advances in language processing enabling their automatic or semi-automatic generation and expansion.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knowledge_graph#cite_note-18)
